newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean government promises worker a better life.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean government promises worker a better life.

text.p: The South Korean government, seeking to end strikes crippling industry, on Friday promised workers a better life with a new bill that would raise living standards and improve employment conditions.

Finance Minister Han Seung-soo told a news conference the bill would be passed soon, but gave no details. He repeated the government's position that strikes sweeping the country were "clearly illegal protests".

"We will send a special bill to improve living standards and employment conditions to the National Assembly as soon as possible," Han said after a meeting of government ministers to discuss the labour crisis.
He said the government would improve vocational training for workers, offer skilled workers greater opportunities and stabilise salaries and living standards.
"We cannot accept for any reason the labour unions' strikes. They are clearly illegal protests," he said.
"The government makes clear it will punish all illegal actions," he said.
